title: Importing an edited .asd or .alc changes the compiled timeline the way the markers say
description:
## Behavior
```gherkin
Feature: Importing warp markers from the DAW

  Background:
    Given the analyzed fixture sample "steady-120.wav" whose analysis puts beat 8 at 4.500 s
    And the score "steady.apr" plays "steady-120.wav" beats 0..16 at tempo 120

  Scenario: Importing an edited .asd changes the compiled timeline
    Given "steady-120.wav.asd" is the DAW-saved file in which beat 8 was moved to 4.600 s
    When I run "apricity import --markers steady-120.wav.asd"
    Then the output says "steady-120.wav: 18 warp markers imported; largest move 100.0 ms at beat 8"
    And "steady-120.wav" has 18 warp markers of mine
    And compiling "steady.apr" pins 4.600 s to beat 8

  Scenario: Importing from an .alc finds the sample from the clip's file reference
    Given "steady-120.alc" saved by the DAW refers to "steady-120.wav"
    When I run "apricity import --markers steady-120.alc"
    Then "steady-120.wav" has warp markers of mine equal to the clip's

  Scenario: --sample names the audio when the reference does not resolve
    Given an .alc whose file reference points to a folder that no longer exists
    When I run "apricity import --markers moved.alc --sample steady-120.wav"
    Then "steady-120.wav" has warp markers of mine equal to the clip's

  Scenario: Importing twice changes nothing
    Given I imported "steady-120.wav.asd"
    When I import it again
    Then the output says "steady-120.wav: warp markers unchanged"

  Scenario: --dry-run shows the change and stores nothing
    When I run "apricity import --markers steady-120.wav.asd --dry-run"
    Then the output lists each marker that would move, with its beat and the move in ms
    And "steady-120.wav" has no warp markers of mine

  Scenario: Importing into a library
    Given a library holding "fixtures/steady-120.wav"
    When I run "apricity import --markers steady-120.wav.asd --library L"
    Then the library has 18 warp markers of mine for that sample
    And pushing the library uploads them like any other marker
```
